doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Al Cohn's advice on New York and arranging
summary: Cohn gave him tips on shortcut arranging, though Allison declined Broadway arranging.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, Al Cohn was a very verbal, witty guy, wasn’t he.
You must have had quite a time exchanging bon mots.
And you said lots of really nice things about Al, what a good person he was. Do you want to talk about him?
I remember we went out to his house, and he took me on right away. He supplied me with a lot of advice about New York.
What did he tell you? What sort of advice?
He was writing mostly for Broadway at the time...
He means what advice did he give you? You said he told you a lot about... Do you remember what advice he gave you?
I remember him telling me how to arrange for Broadway, and I wasn’t about to do that. But he told me how to shortcut arrangements, and what he was doing...
So he showed you arranging craft things...
